# Documentation Instructions

- Keep docs aligned with current behavior; update docs in the same change as code updates.
- Document public APIs, config variables, and operational runbooks clearly.
- Include examples only when they are executable and verified.
- Prefer concise, task-oriented sections: purpose, prerequisites, steps, validation.
- Record security-sensitive behavior and safe usage constraints explicitly.
- Avoid leaking internal secrets, tokens, customer data, or private URLs in docs.
- Add migration notes when behavior, defaults, or interfaces change.
- Use consistent terminology and naming with the codebase.
- Mark deprecated behavior with removal timelines and alternatives.
- Validate links and command snippets before finalizing changes.
